why: A HIGH finding where firstName returns the last name instead of the first name (index [1] instead of [0]), and a MEDIUM finding where the test assertion is too loose to catch this bug.

findings.title: `firstName` returns the last name instead of the first name
findings.body:
The function `firstName` uses `split(" ")[1]` which accesses the second word, not the first. For input "Ada Lovelace", this returns "Lovelace" instead of "Ada". The comment correctly says "first name" but the implementation is wrong.

Fix: change `[1]` to `[0]` to return the first word.

findings.title: Test uses loose regex that doesn't verify the name output
findings.body:
The test uses `/^Welcome back, /` which only checks the prefix. It would pass even if `welcomeBack` returned "Welcome back, undefined!" or "Welcome back, !" (empty name). This loose assertion allowed the firstName bug to go undetected.

Fix: verify the actual name, e.g., `toBe("Welcome back, Ada!")`.
